results.title: Photos from ‘Democracy Is Not for Sale’ dialogue in Oti Region
results.content: JoyNews has taken its Democracy Is Not for Sale dialogue to Dambai in the Oti Region, bringing together stakeholders and members of the public to examine the growing influence of money in Ghana’s electoral process. The engagement, held at the Dambai College of Education on Friday, November 13, focused on vote buying, political financing and the implications of financial inducements for the country’s democratic development. The dialogue provided a platform for participants to reflect on how money influences voting decisions, the factors that make voters vulnerable to inducements and the need to protect the integrity of elections. A key concern surrounding vote buying is its potential to undermine the freedom of voters to make independent choices and weaken public confidence in the electoral process. results.title: Sam Jonah calls on Mahama to restore Gen Acheampong’s military rank, says Ghana must correct injustice of 1979 execution
results.content: Business magnate and former AngloGold Ashanti Chairman, Sir Sam Jonah, has called on President John Mahama and the Ghana Armed Forces to restore the military rank of former Head of State, General Ignatius Kutu Acheampong, arguing that his execution in 1979 without trial should not permanently erase his military identity and years of service.

results.title: Bawumia pledges to make agriculture a national security priority
results.content: New Patriotic Party (NPP) flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia has pledged to make agriculture a national security priority if elected President, citing challenges facing rice farmers and the need to strengthen Ghana’s food security. Speaking to rice farmers at Asutsuare in the Shai-Osudoku District, Dr Bawumia said his proposed government would adopt a more deliberate approach to agricultural development, given the sector’s importance to national survival and economic stability. He identified difficulties accessing fertiliser, inadequate irrigation infrastructure and the lack of reliable markets for locally produced rice as some of the challenges requiring urgent attention. Some farmers who interacted with him said they had taken loans to expand production but were struggling to recover their investments because buyers were not purchasing their produce.

results.title: Human rights and Democratic futures: Reflections from West and Central Africa
results.content: There is a fundamental question confronting the human rights movement in Africa today: How do we defend human rights in societies where many citizens increasingly question whether democracy, constitutionalism, and the institutions established to protect their rights are delivering meaningful improvements in their lives? This question is particularly urgent in West and Central Africa, where democratic aspirations coexist with military interventions, constitutional controversies, violent extremism, economic exclusion, and growing pressures on civic freedoms. Yet these same regions are also home to extraordinary traditions of civic resistance, community solidarity, constitutional activism, women's leadership, and youth mobilisation.
